headline: Gold prices rise by 1,633 BDT per bhori in Bangladesh
summary: The price of 22-carat gold has increased due to rising global market trends, reaching 247,743 BDT per bhori.
details: The price of high-quality 22-carat gold in Bangladesh has increased by 1,633 BDT per bhori, effective from 10 AM today, Tuesday.
The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) announced the price hike up to the local market price of 'Tejabi' gold, aligning with global market trends.
Following the increase, 22-carat gold now costs 247,743 BDT per bhori. 21-carat gold is priced at 236,604 BDT, while 18-carat gold is 203,187 BDT.
Traditional gold is now priced at 165,920 BDT per bhori. Silver prices remain unchanged.
This follows a previous increase on August 22, where prices rose by a maximum of 5,482 BDT per bhori. In total, gold prices have risen by 7,115 BDT per bhori since last Saturday.
The price hike is driven by a falling US dollar, uncertainty regarding US interest rates, and increased investor demand for gold globally.
According to Reuters, gold prices have exceeded the 200-day average of $4,513 per ounce. GoldPrice.org reports current prices at $4,625 per ounce.
Historically, gold prices in Bangladesh reached a peak of 286,000 BDT per bhori on January 29 of this year.
caption:

Following the increase, 22-carat gold now costs 247,743 BDT per bhori. 21-carat gold is priced at 236,604 BDT, while 18-carat gold is 203,187 BDT.

Traditional gold is now priced at 165,920 BDT per bhori. Silver prices remain unchanged.

This follows a previous increase on August 22, where prices rose by a maximum of 5,482 BDT per bhori. In total, gold prices have risen by 7,115 BDT per bhori since last Saturday.

The price hike is driven by a falling US dollar, uncertainty regarding US interest rates, and increased investor demand for gold globally.

According to Reuters, gold prices have exceeded the 200-day average of $4,513 per ounce. GoldPrice.org reports current prices at $4,625 per ounce.

Historically, gold prices in Bangladesh reached a peak of 286,000 BDT per bhori on January 29 of this year.

headline_marked: Sammilito Islami Bank: [[Depositors can withdraw money from Sept 1]]
headline: Sammilito Islami Bank: Depositors can withdraw money from Sept 1
summary: Bangladesh Bank Governor confirms no profit haircut for depositors as the bank works to resume normal operations.
details: Bangladesh Bank Governor Md Mostaqur Rahman has instructed Sammilito Islami Bank to clearly inform all depositors that there will be no haircut on their profits.
The directive came during a meeting in Dhaka between the governor and the bank's chairman, Kazi Shairul Hasan, and managing director, Abedur Rahman Sikder.
The governor noted that while the finance minister had already announced in Parliament that profits would not be cut, some ambiguity still existed among depositors.
Starting September 1, individual depositors will be able to withdraw principal amounts from Al-Wadiyah current accounts, Mudaraba savings accounts, and Mudaraba term deposits.
Sammilito Islami Bank PLC, which began as the country's largest state-owned Islamic bank with a capital of Tk 35,000 crore, is now taking steps to resume all normal banking activities.
Deputy Governors Md Habibur Rahman, Md Kabir Ahmed, Md Sarwar Hossain, and Md Anisur Rahman were also present at the meeting to oversee the progress.
caption:
No profit cuts for depositors! Sammilito Islami Bank customers can start withdrawing their funds from September 1.

Bangladesh Bank Governor Md Mostaqur Rahman has instructed Sammilito Islami Bank to clearly inform all depositors that there will be no haircut on their profits.

The directive came during a meeting in Dhaka between the governor and the bank's chairman, Kazi Shairul Hasan, and managing director, Abedur Rahman Sikder.

The governor noted that while the finance minister had already announced in Parliament that profits would not be cut, some ambiguity still existed among depositors.

Starting September 1, individual depositors will be able to withdraw principal amounts from Al-Wadiyah current accounts, Mudaraba savings accounts, and Mudaraba term deposits.

Sammilito Islami Bank PLC, which began as the country's largest state-owned Islamic bank with a capital of Tk 35,000 crore, is now taking steps to resume all normal banking activities.

Deputy Governors Md Habibur Rahman, Md Kabir Ahmed, Md Sarwar Hossain, and Md Anisur Rahman were also present at the meeting to oversee the progress.
